examples.rule: Route exact brand copy and high-value typography to a post-composite text layer unless the generation is explicitly being used as a text-risk experiment.
examples.when_to_use: Logos, watch dials, signage, packaging, license plates, and UI screens.
examples.why_it_matters: Studio signs and watch dials produced omissions or gibberish; only selected variants held short text reliably.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text Strategy selector: native generation, reserved blank plate, or post-composite

examples.rule: Route exact brand names, disclosure overlays, and other mandatory text to a deterministic post-render text layer.
examples.when_to_use: Branded products, legal disclosures, signs, UI, and any exact-copy requirement.
examples.why_it_matters: Dryden/Pathfinder and Million Dollar Studio text repeatedly mutated or disappeared despite explicit wording.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Deterministic Text And Disclosure Pass

examples.rule: Route exact brand or overlay copy to a typography-safe post layer instead of asking the generator to render it in-scene.
examples.when_to_use: Packaging, end cards, logos, engravings, and UI screens.
examples.why_it_matters: Generated copy produced FIT FUE, Focus.reve, duplicate words, and warped DRYDEN lettering.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text Fidelity mode: suppress generated text, reserve safe area, then composite approved copy.

examples.rule: Route exact brand text, subtitles, labels, and URLs to a deterministic overlay unless text rendering is itself the experiment.
examples.when_to_use: Logos, product labels, software promo cards, subtitles, packaging, and branded installations.
examples.why_it_matters: Porsche crest details, APEX/APX/APEZ labels, Runway naming, influencer subtitles, and office signage drifted or became gibberish; the coffee label was a rare success, not reliable proof.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Render-plate plus deterministic typography/logo compositor with OCR gate.

examples.rule: Route exact brand text to an supplied label asset or post-render compositor; do not depend on generative lettering for approval-critical names.
examples.when_to_use: Any pack shot, sachet, bottle, bag, logo, or sign requiring exact spelling.
examples.why_it_matters: FitFuel became variants such as Fituel, FIFULL, or vertically distorted gibberish in every branded render.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Brand-safe label compositor and required reference-asset slot.

examples.rule: Route exact campaign copy and disclosure text to deterministic post-render compositing instead of asking the video model to draw it.
examples.when_to_use: Any prompt containing required brand, legal, location, launch, or disclosure copy.
examples.why_it_matters: All ten advertising variants with requested copy produced misspellings, omissions, or changing pseudo-text even when the underlying environment was strong.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text-safe render route that strips exact copy from generation, reserves a composition-safe text zone, and emits a deterministic overlay specification.

examples.rule: Route exact copy, brand names, street signs, and slogans to post-compositing over a generated text-safe plate.
examples.when_to_use: Any shot where wording is a release-critical requirement.
examples.why_it_matters: Generated lettering was absent, malformed, or temporally unstable across the AI teaser, PATHFINDER, Calle Soledad, and restaurant-title prompts.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Exact-copy compositor route with reserved negative-space mask

examples.rule: Route exact hero copy, headlines, task labels, and brand-book names to a deterministic typography overlay rather than asking the video model to draw text.
examples.when_to_use: Any shot whose success depends on exact spelling, punctuation, capitalization, or multi-line readability.
examples.why_it_matters: All four newspaper variants failed the target sentence, and multiple chair, monitor, and book variants produced malformed or temporally changing text.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Exact Text Overlay mode with font, case, placement, fade timing, and safe-area controls.

examples.rule: Route macro-liquid prompts through a named material model instead of a generic pour or droplet instruction.
examples.when_to_use: Crema, honey, beer condensation, foam, syrup, or any close fluid interaction.
examples.why_it_matters: Crema remained coherent when treated as a patterned surface, while honey and condensation frequently became glassy, spherical, or topology-changing.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Material Physics Mode with presets for crema advection, honey viscosity, condensation adhesion, and foam impact.

examples.rule: Route named brand marks and printed copy to supplied assets or post-render compositing instead of generative reconstruction.
examples.when_to_use: Whenever a logo, package mark, or readable microcopy is delivery-critical.
examples.why_it_matters: Starbucks-style cup geometry was often stable, but logos were approximate and printed text became gibberish.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Brand asset lock and composite pass

examples.rule: Route readable hero packaging through a typography-safe path instead of free-generating label copy.
examples.when_to_use: Any shot where a jar, tub, phone, title card, or other text-bearing surface occupies close-up or hero scale.
examples.why_it_matters: This batch repeatedly produced attractive packshots whose invented or mutating labels made them unusable.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Label-safe mode with reference-art upload, text-free generation, and deterministic post-composite routing.

examples.rule: Route readable typography, logos, plates, labels, and end cards to deterministic post-production.
examples.when_to_use: Any deliverable where text must be trusted.
examples.why_it_matters: Generated packaging, title cards, plates, retailer copy, and Devanagari-like lettering repeatedly drifted or became gibberish.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text-safe mode that generates clean plates and emits a compositing manifest for real typography.

examples.rule: Route simple, center-locked product actions to generation before complex multi-actor or multi-vehicle choreography.
examples.when_to_use: Use for orbital reveals, flat lays, reach-and-lift actions, interior details, and fixed packshots.
examples.why_it_matters: The cleanest records constrained subject count, environment, and action while preserving an obvious visual proof beat.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Complexity router that recommends the lowest-risk shot grammar for the requested proof.

examples.rule: Route text, maps, clocks, dashboards, and device screens through a semantic-fidelity mode that locks layout and factual geometry before adding camera motion.
examples.when_to_use: Any concept whose meaning depends on readable labels, geographic topology, clock numerals, routes, charts, or persistent UI.
examples.why_it_matters: The batch repeatedly produced attractive shells with unusable semantic surfaces: continents morphed, clock numerals changed, and interface tiles regenerated.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Semantic Surface Lock preset with text-free fallback, map topology lock, numeral lock, and persistent UI reference inputs.

examples.rule: Separate intentional chromatic face transformation from identity-preserving portrait mode.
examples.when_to_use: Surreal fashion, identity graphics, projected-color portraits, and metamorphosis concepts.
examples.why_it_matters: A featureless graphic mask remained coherent, but portraits that retained facial features suffered identity and anatomy drift as color fields moved.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Face Transform selector: graphic mask, projected color, anatomy morph, or identity lock.

examples.rule: Separate prompt adherence from visual quality and reject subject substitution even when the substitute footage is attractive.
examples.when_to_use: All generations, with a hard subject/action gate for documentary, product, and stunt briefs.
examples.why_it_matters: One boxer brief returned a bird interaction, while one excellent robotic-eye render omitted the requested text overlay entirely.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Dual-axis QC: visual craft score plus independent instruction-compliance score with hard subject gates.

examples.rule: Separate visible creative direction from unprovable camera, speed, price, provenance and acoustic claims.
examples.when_to_use: Any prompt containing exact equipment, measured performance, named locations or technical certifications.
examples.why_it_matters: Frames could support warm backlight, parallel tracking or a mountain pass, but not 490.48 km/h, a specific sensor, Michelin status or acoustic isolation mass.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Claim Ceiling lint that labels prompt clauses as visually testable, metadata-only or provider/runtime proof required.

examples.rule: Simple nature b-roll prompts perform best when they name foreground texture plus mood.
examples.when_to_use: Beach, forest, water, sky, and ambient b-roll generation.
examples.why_it_matters: Sunset beach renders were stable; the most distinctive ones included visible foam, wet sand, or reflection paths.
examples.os_feature_candidate: B-roll texture enhancer that adds one foreground material and one light-reflection cue.

examples.rule: Specify fluid source, viscosity range, contact surface, maximum volume, and forbidden envelope shapes.
examples.when_to_use: Use for steam, syrup, coffee pours, smoke, sauces, and other deformable materials.
examples.why_it_matters: Steam became ribbon-like and syrup inflated into glass-like shells or unrealistically broad sheets.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Fluid-physics prompt module with viscosity and collision guards.

examples.rule: Specify material start, transfer path, and end state for granular or liquid ingredients.
examples.when_to_use: Coffee grounds, beans, powders, liquids, or any visible material transformation.
examples.why_it_matters: Grounds appeared in piles, formed graphic spirals, vanished, or changed material without plausible contact.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Material-physics prompt block with conservation and contact requirements.

examples.rule: Specify one continuous action with explicit start, transition, and end states; prohibit teleporting between action states.
examples.when_to_use: Leaps, climbs, water entries, rides, chases, and other creature stunts.
examples.why_it_matters: The weakest renders skipped launch, contact, landing, or water-entry beats and replaced them with abrupt position or state changes.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Action State Compiler

examples.rule: Specify one primary camera motion and one resolved endpoint for short jewelry clips.
examples.when_to_use: Single-product necklace, pendant, ring, or earring beauty shots.
examples.why_it_matters: Seventeen clips repeated a still or offered negligible crop drift, while controlled push-ins, slides, and orbits produced the clearest temporal value.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Motion Intent selector with Push In, Lateral Slide, Orbit, and Context Reveal presets

examples.rule: Specify one visible action with direction, contact point, start state, and end state.
examples.when_to_use: Short food, product, and miniature-process videos.
examples.why_it_matters: Single-action pours and oven beats were more coherent than prompts listing many simultaneous activities.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Action Vector Builder

examples.rule: Specify terminal states with a hold requirement and prohibit reversion after the climax.
examples.when_to_use: White-outs, reveals, destruction, fades, transformations, and loop endpoints.
examples.why_it_matters: One neural render flashed white in the middle and returned to the web, while two never reached the required white ending.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Terminal-state contract with onset timestamp, hold duration, and no-reversion flag.

examples.rule: Specify three to five visibly distinct beats built around changes in scale, material, or viewpoint; do not rely on camera-spec volume to create progression.
examples.when_to_use: Automotive, food-process, and short narrative prompts that need a complete arc in 10-15 seconds.
examples.why_it_matters: The strongest renders clearly changed what the viewer could inspect, while several maximal prompts repeated nearly identical compositions.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Beat-density planner with a visible-change test for every beat.

examples.rule: Split dense multi-beat prompts into one visually testable action per shot and require an explicit hard-cut checklist before generation.
examples.when_to_use: Five-second sequences containing a title card, handshake, walk-away, hug, selfie, or screen insert.
examples.why_it_matters: Variants routinely reversed shot order, merged interactions onto the chair, or stopped before the final beat.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Beat Budget validator that warns when requested cuts and actions exceed the available seconds.

examples.rule: Split long stunt prose into independently verifiable shot cards.
examples.when_to_use: Sequences with more than three irreversible physical beats, multiple locations, or second-by-second timing.
examples.why_it_matters: Both 15-second rooftop prompts delivered only fragments; one substituted a broken-rooftop fall and the other stopped after a gravel-recess landing.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Duration-aware stunt beat splitter with one proof frame and continuity checksum per shot card.

examples.rule: Split multi-beat human-product narratives into separately renderable shots before generation.
examples.when_to_use: When a short render asks for a character, environment, prop transformation, camera sequence, emotional arc, and interface change together.
examples.why_it_matters: All four diplomat variants collapsed to bonsai beauty shots and omitted the human, treaties, emotion, and product interface.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Prompt complexity budget with automatic beat splitting

examples.rule: State a continuity budget for people, cups, and props before generating group scenes.
examples.when_to_use: Family rituals, team culture, tasting games, and competitions.
examples.why_it_matters: Busy scenes accumulated hand, identity, cup-count, and placement drift.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Continuity budget selector

examples.rule: State one camera invariant and one geometric relationship in plain language when the effect depends on alignment.
examples.when_to_use: Optical illusions, logo completion, compositing, and front-axis transformations.
examples.why_it_matters: The horse-and-crest render preserved front-facing alignment and completed the negative-space effect across every sample.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Invariant pinning for camera axis, subject center, scale ratio, and forbidden views.

examples.rule: State one immutable identity and one continuity lock for every persistent hero prop or foreground object.
examples.when_to_use: Product macros, street tracking shots, and any sequence where small geometry remains visible across time.
examples.why_it_matters: Watch links, watch faces, manhole covers, and steam sources changed shape, count, or location between sampled frames.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Persistent-object continuity contract

examples.rule: State one measurable motion arc and require visible start, midpoint, and payoff states.
examples.when_to_use: Abstract loops, product compression demos, workspace b-roll, pours, and other prompts vulnerable to static-frame output.
examples.why_it_matters: Several clips looked polished as stills but showed insufficient evolution across five temporal samples.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Motion Coverage checker using frame-delta thresholds plus semantic start/mid/end confirmation.

examples.rule: State persistent geometry invariants and contact-point ownership explicitly: same product, same part layout, same hand, same vessel, and same source-to-target connection across every frame.
examples.when_to_use: Use for products, food actions, tools, hands, liquids, and macro object shots.
examples.why_it_matters: Beans regenerated during orbits, watches changed models, and coffee streams detached from their source vessels.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Continuity invariant editor for product geometry, contact points, hand ownership, and no-morph constraints.

examples.rule: State prop ownership and attachment explicitly: named character, named hand, fixed silhouette, and no body overlap.
examples.when_to_use: Any close-up or over-the-shoulder scene with a hand-held hero prop.
examples.why_it_matters: The compass repeatedly changed from disk to orb, floated over the body, or fused with Evelyn's head despite otherwise strong library imagery.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Prop continuity block with shape reference, hand assignment, screen position, and forbidden overlaps.

examples.rule: State topology explicitly for impossible-in-miniature concepts: inside the vessel, below the rim, physically contained, exterior plain, and camera angle revealing the interior.
examples.when_to_use: Contained worlds, cutaways, cross-sections, or interior illusions that could be misread as printed surface decoration.
examples.why_it_matters: All stormy-sea variants rendered ocean artwork on the mug exterior instead of a tempest contained inside it.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Concept-topology controls for inside, outside, cutaway, printed-on, and physically-contained relationships.

examples.rule: Strip workflow commentary, cost claims, and unrenderable numerical claims before generation.
examples.when_to_use: Any prompt assembled from research notes, framework output, or model conversation.
examples.why_it_matters: Meta-instructions and cost prose consumed prompt budget without adding visible evidence and made intent harder to recover.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Prompt sanitizer that classifies creative direction, production metadata, claims, and removable chatter.

examples.rule: Suppress generated words and logos unless a downstream text-replacement pass is planned.
examples.when_to_use: Cafe venues, challenges, packaging, uniforms, and branded campaigns.
examples.why_it_matters: Signage, package labels, cup marks, and aprons repeatedly mutated into unusable text.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text-risk guard plus clean-plate export

examples.rule: Translate emotional titles into a required visible action contract.
examples.when_to_use: Titles such as 'Hopeful Morning Sip' or any concept whose key verb must be shown.
examples.why_it_matters: Four sip-titled renders showed only jar presentation, with no cup, liquid, or sip.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Required-beat checklist generated from title verbs and nouns before rendering.

examples.rule: Treat exact aspect ratio and exact brand text as hard render contracts, not descriptive prose.
examples.when_to_use: Launch idents, title cards, product logos, signage, interfaces, and any format-specific delivery.
examples.why_it_matters: All four AI-studio variants were landscape instead of 9:16 and all corrupted the requested wordmark; travel signs also drifted.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Format and Typography Lock that routes exact text to deterministic compositing

examples.rule: Treat exact brand typography as a compositing requirement, not a free-generation detail.
examples.when_to_use: Use for logos, model names, dial copy, engravings, packaging, or any legibility-critical text.
examples.why_it_matters: Metal and camera rendering stayed strong while DRYDEN and AUTOMATIC duplicated, misspelled, or morphed across frames.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text-safe route with blank plate generation plus tracked typography overlay.

examples.rule: Treat exact readable text and semantic icon pairing as hard constraints.
examples.when_to_use: Workbooks, labels, interfaces, packaging, and educational content.
examples.why_it_matters: Plausible page layouts still failed when titles became gibberish or a goose instruction rendered as a duck-like icon.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Typography And Semantic Fidelity Gate

examples.rule: Treat exact readable text as a post-production layer unless the render engine has a verified text-safe path.
examples.when_to_use: Brand books, signs, plates, billboards, end cards, sponsor graphics, and product marks.
examples.why_it_matters: Generated text repeatedly became malformed even when the surrounding imagery was usable.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text Risk Router that replaces in-render copy with tracked blank surfaces and overlay specs

examples.rule: Treat exact text, labels, plates, road markings, and end cards as deterministic post-render assets.
examples.when_to_use: Any product, brand, price, legal copy, subtitle, UI, road sign, or campaign end card.
examples.why_it_matters: Bottle labels, plaque copy, plates, road text, and the ESCAPE GRAVITY end card drifted even when the imagery was otherwise strong.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Exact Copy Post-Compose Router

examples.rule: Treat generated copy as a placeholder unless a rendered text check passes.
examples.when_to_use: End cards, supers, packaging labels, dashboards, and in-world signage.
examples.why_it_matters: Several otherwise usable films failed on gibberish logos, brand lines, or product labels.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Typography Safety toggle that defaults to clean plates plus post-production text overlays.

examples.rule: Treat logos, packaging labels, scoreboards, and interface copy as post-composited text unless exact text rendering is separately verified.
examples.when_to_use: Branded domestic ads and gaming-reaction composites.
examples.why_it_matters: Small brand and game UI text was present but not reliably legible in delivered frames.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text-Safe Render mode with post-composite overlays

examples.rule: Treat precision products as topology-locked: explicitly require fixed hands, indices, numerals, prongs, strands, and complications across every frame.
examples.when_to_use: Watches and jewelry with small rigid components.
examples.why_it_matters: Attractive watch and necklace surfaces repeatedly failed because rigid furniture migrated, duplicated, or reconfigured.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Precision Topology Lock and small-component continuity checklist.

examples.rule: Treat readable logos, plates, gauges, URLs, and end cards as post-production layers, not generative image content.
examples.when_to_use: Brand films, instrument macros, food end cards, license plates, signage, or any shot where text carries meaning.
examples.why_it_matters: Generated typography repeatedly warped even when the surrounding image was commercially strong.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Typography handoff mode that generates clean plates and exports editable text-overlay specifications.

examples.rule: Treat readable text and third-party identity as gated assets, never incidental generated texture.
examples.when_to_use: Signs, notes, screens, logos, watermarks, jerseys, and branded product scenes.
examples.why_it_matters: Malformed signage, interface text, jersey marks, and a visible Vitabean watermark survived into otherwise usable shots.
examples.os_feature_candidate: Text and Brand Lock with exact asset upload, OCR review, and reject-or-repair routing.

examples.rule: Treat readable text, logos, equations, clocks, and branded marks as a separate compositing layer instead of asking the video model to preserve them in-scene.

examples.visible_symptom: Gas bubbles become chrome-like solid clusters, rocks, or impossible chains.

examples.visible_symptom: Popcorn kernels crawl, fruit bodies intersect, and hands or tools lose contact geometry.

examples.visible_symptom: Worker count, identity, limbs, tools, or pose changes between sampled frames.

examples.visible_symptom: Chef or passenger count, faces, limbs, poses, and tool ownership change across frames.

examples.visible_symptom: Hands, faces, cups, tools, costumes, and figure counts change between samples.

examples.visible_symptom: Human hands or giant knives take over, or one chef changes scale relative to peers.

examples.visible_symptom: Ingredients float, stems grow, supports vanish, rice does not displace, and tiny character identities drift.

examples.visible_symptom: Full-size hands pick up characters, dominate tools, or become the primary cook.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: No full-size hands or people in frame; all hero actions performed by a fixed-count miniature crew.

examples.visible_symptom: Miniature workers coexist with full-size hands and tools, reducing workers to decorative scale cues.

examples.visible_symptom: One person persists while mug color, handle count, and geometry transform continuously.

examples.visible_symptom: Underexposure, crushed blacks, haze, or extreme shallow focus hides the subject and process.

examples.visible_symptom: One attractive setup replaces the required aerial, observer reveal, reaction close-up, or blackout.

examples.visible_symptom: One or more required materials cannot be distinguished and deformable subjects lose stable geometry.

examples.visible_symptom: Second vehicles vanish, swap models, intersect architecture, or leave the payoff shot empty.

examples.visible_symptom: Five sampled frames are nearly identical except for minor wave, mist, or framing changes.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify a measurable camera move or foreground motion event with start and end states.

examples.visible_symptom: A prompt explicitly forbids steam or geometry errors, yet the render shows over-dense steam and morphing meat.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Translate negative constraints into positive state invariants and a visible QC checklist rather than relying on repeated NO clauses.

examples.visible_symptom: Splash phases reset, liquid misses the vessel, foam jumps, or cheese behaves as straight wires.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare one direction of state change, enforce vessel contact or strand attachment, and require continuous volume conservation.

examples.visible_symptom: Bean piles regenerate, watch dials change model, and component layouts mutate during camera motion.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use a reference image and lock exact object silhouette, material, part count, part positions, and no-regeneration continuity.

examples.visible_symptom: People change count or identity after passing behind trees, coats, or foreground pedestrians.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Preserve exact subject count and wardrobe through occlusion; no character replacement or merge behind foreground objects.

examples.visible_symptom: Vertical, square, or 4:3 prompts repeatedly return horizontal frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Bind aspect outside prose as a renderer parameter and reject dimension mismatch before QC.

examples.visible_symptom: Decade changes, orange fire, extreme-sport scenes, or interface demonstrations never appear.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: One shot card per environment or era; require a delivered-beat checklist before assembly.

examples.visible_symptom: Major jumps, landings, rolls, and shutter beats vanish or are replaced by a fall into unrelated geometry.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: One obstacle per shot; require takeoff, clearance, landing, and recovery before routing to the next obstacle.

examples.visible_symptom: Neon, sunset, or desert scenes clip highlights, crush shadows, or lose natural material separation.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Preserve highlight rolloff and shadow detail, cap saturation, and hold one exposure profile for the full shot.

examples.visible_symptom: Body panels detach, wheels separate, shell liquefies or the final object becomes unreadable.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Keep a complete invariant base mesh visible; confine particles to a bounded rear or surface mask; forbid effect contact with wheels, windows and frontal identity.

examples.visible_symptom: Predator anatomy deforms, limbs become ambiguous, or takeoff-contact-landing chains disappear.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Separate action into initiation, contact, and resolution shots with anatomy and support-point checks.

examples.failure: Persistent corner mark or provider-like glyph
examples.visible_symptom: Small changing line/glyph or knot icon appears at the lower-right in 42 reviewed records; origin is UNKNOWN.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Add a clean-plate/export verification step and reject any unapproved corner mark; do not assume prompt suppression can remove provider-owned marks.

examples.visible_symptom: A small generator mark appears at lower right in every reviewed record.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Treat watermark-free source output or approved removal/compositing as a hard delivery gate before gold classification.

examples.visible_symptom: Hero links, manholes, signs, steam sources, or facial seams change shape, count, or position.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare immutable object ID, count, geometry, material, and screen location; reject regenerated replacements.

examples.visible_symptom: The displayed viewpoint changes independently of the visible phone position or duplicates the subject identity.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock screen content to a rendered camera transform and freeze the captured image after the shutter beat.

examples.visible_symptom: Ribs hang as a rigid vertical curtain, characters float by a human grip, or fisheye roll makes the world appear spherical.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: State support, gravity, attachment, and maximum lens distortion; require one plausible support path for every suspended object.

examples.visible_symptom: Prompt specifies exact fluid or stunt mechanics, but delivered geometry is impossible or the event is not shown.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Describe observable contact geometry and conservation rules; score only the rendered event, never numerical prompt claims.

examples.visible_symptom: Detached duplicate wheel, floating car without support, malformed prey or unsupported fragments.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare support/contact constraints and conservation rules; reject duplicate wheels, floating mass and anatomy changes in QC.

examples.visible_symptom: Watch parts interpenetrate, a product changes identity, or fluid clings and crawls unnaturally.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock topology and material volume; simplify to one physical event with baseline, trigger, peak and settle beats.

examples.visible_symptom: Front-wheel smoke on rear-drive burnouts, cars nearly entering walls, and people standing in active jet taxi paths.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare drive axle, contact forces, clearances, safety perimeter, and forbidden occupancy zones; add a physics/safety review gate.

examples.visible_symptom: Impossible proximity, body intersections, or continuity jumps make an action unreadable even when the premise is cinematic.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Reduce the action to one stunt, preserve screen direction, and require a wide geography frame before close impact coverage.

examples.failure: Plastic, diseased, or paint-like food material
examples.visible_symptom: Sauce becomes skin-like bumps, paneer glaze becomes embossed plastic, or spinach puree resembles glossy paint.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use food-specific roughness, pores, moisture, char, and viscosity; prohibit plastic sheen, skin-like nodules, embossed repeats, and perfectly concentric puree.

examples.visible_symptom: Spices become cohesive sheets, rings, or smooth spirals instead of granular falls.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify loose independent grains, gravity-led fall, turbulent breakup, bowl contact, dust rebound, and no ribbon or cloth-like cohesion.

examples.visible_symptom: Watch hands, indices, numerals, gems, prongs, or strands move, duplicate, or reform.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Keep every rigid component fixed in count, placement, orientation, attachment, and readable identity across all frames; camera motion only.

examples.visible_symptom: Watch hands, gears, phone buttons, bottle facets, controls, and handbag hardware change topology between frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: One immutable product CAD-like identity; fixed component count, position, dimensions, and finish across every frame.

examples.visible_symptom: Sachet pours clear liquid or coffee grounds land on a drip tray instead of a portafilter.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Name source, material state, target receptacle, and forbidden wrong surface in one isolated action shot.

examples.visible_symptom: Hardware, complications, badges, fascia, or accessories change across angles.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use a fixed product reference, immutable component checklist, and separately composited hero plate.

examples.visible_symptom: Pet-bed rim shape changes, support state is ambiguous, or the requested pose disappears.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock silhouette, seams, support state, air gap, and subject pose separately; allow only camera change.

examples.visible_symptom: Cup height, rim, opacity, and internal black panels change between frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock one product silhouette, explicit layer stack, fixed rim diameter, fixed transparency, and no transformation unless each assembly beat is storyboarded.

examples.visible_symptom: Watch dial, complication, bracelet, car body, or brand geometry changes across angles.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Bind every shot to one product reference and repeat immutable dial, case, strap, wheel, grille, and badge descriptors.

examples.visible_symptom: Package window, height, folds, or branding surface changes without a physical mechanism.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock silhouette and construction details across every frame; forbid materialization, morphing, and unprompted redesign.

examples.visible_symptom: Vehicle fascia, bottle proportions, garment construction, or human identity changes between angles.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use immutable reference images, angle checkpoints, and no-unmotivated-identity-change constraints.

examples.visible_symptom: A jar appears, vanishes, duplicates, or jumps from background to oversized foreground without handling or camera motivation.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Keep one product at a fixed marked location, or call for an explicit hard cut to a separate packshot; prohibit in-shot appearance, duplication, or scale change.

examples.visible_symptom: Rendered subject has no grounding in the provided prompt because the prompt is meta-analysis or code.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Extract only the final scene directive; reject preamble, code blocks, framework analysis, and conversational residue.

examples.repair: Reserve a close-up product frame before environmental beauty beats and score product absence as a hard miss.

examples.failure: Prompt density hides the essential beat
examples.visible_symptom: Rich material and camera prose renders an attractive held image while the core nod, ignition, look-back, or recovery never occurs.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Place a short MUST-SHOW beat list before style prose and reserve explicit frame budget for each beat.

examples.visible_symptom: Fifteen-second or eight-beat direction forced into five seconds, and ultra-widescreen camera language delivered vertically.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Validate requested beat count and aspect against render duration before generation; reject or simplify incompatible briefs.

examples.visible_symptom: Workers, clothing, locations, factory context, logo payoff, and assembly operations disappear despite long timestamped prompts.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Split into one-shot prompts and verify each required beat before edit assembly.

examples.visible_symptom: Long multi-action prompts reduce to a static tableau or a single attractive motif while dropping characters, actions, text, and payoff.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Split into independent shots with one action each and require a checklist of visible beats before synthesis.

examples.visible_symptom: Horizontal prompts render as portrait or portrait prompts contain horizontal letterboxed footage.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Validate encoded dimensions before review and route mismatches to crop/re-render rather than accepting composition loss.

examples.visible_symptom: The coffee container changes category, lid design, scale, fill, or label between frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Repeat immutable prop geometry and forbid handles, lid changes, fill changes, and label redesign except when explicitly storyboarded.

examples.failure: Prop materialization, disappearance, or role substitution
examples.visible_symptom: Packages vanish, cups appear, wrappers become drinks, or a card becomes a knife.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare the complete prop inventory and require explicit cuts for every add, remove, or role change.

examples.visible_symptom: A small generator logo or tick pattern remains in the lower-right corner.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use a watermark-free export path or crop only when composition and legal policy permit; never mark gold before automated corner inspection.

examples.visible_symptom: Visible Sora marks jump between corners around an otherwise clean bottle pack shot.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Reject watermarked exports before scoring and route to an approved clean-output path.

examples.visible_symptom: Cup vanishes mid-pour, smoke floats without a source car, or vapor originates from implausible body regions.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Bind every material effect to one named source and receiver; require both remain visible through the entire interaction.

examples.visible_symptom: The character, brick geometry, and color system strongly resemble a protected toy brand even without a readable logo.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use original modular toy proportions, non-infringing connector geometry, custom face language, and a distinct palette.

examples.failure: Repeated small actors or objects drift and disappear
examples.visible_symptom: Workers, terminals, tools, and crowds soften, change count, or vanish while the hero remains stable.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Cap repeated actor count, enlarge critical actors, and render background population as separate locked plates when possible.

examples.failure: Requested action omitted or reduced to a static hold
examples.visible_symptom: Clasp never cycles, aircraft hovers, montage stays on one subject, or beans fail to cascade.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify start state, visible transition, end state, and minimum screen-space or mechanism delta.

examples.failure: Requested text made of steam/light does not form reliably
examples.repair: Use post-composited particle typography or route to tabletop/surface text fallback if exact readability is required.

examples.failure: Requested transformation remains a static plate
examples.visible_symptom: Near-identical sampled frames with no seed release, no gesture, or no state change.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Define measurable frame-state deltas: intact percentage, detached count, destination region, and final remainder.

examples.visible_symptom: Acrobat limbs fuse, ropes change attachment, and bodies appear unsupported.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use one performer, one apparatus, a fixed grip, a readable pendulum arc, and no intersecting rigging.

examples.failure: Rigid or anatomical identity morphs over time
examples.visible_symptom: Airframes, antlers, faces, hands, and tiny-character bodies change geometry between frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use one identity reference, reduce simultaneous motion, and run temporal anchor checks on rigid silhouettes and anatomy.

examples.visible_symptom: Watch dial color, hand geometry, pivots, bezel marks, bracelet type, or model text changes across frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock one reference product, enumerate immutable geometry, remove text from generation, and use one simple camera move.

examples.visible_symptom: A liquid swirl appears on the desk and the sachet arrives after the supposed mixture.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Enforce ordered states: sealed sachet, tear, pour into cup, contained swirl, steam, sip, clarity; no liquid outside vessel.

examples.visible_symptom: Full-size hands replace tiny agents, workers move below the target, or a new shot abandons the miniature worksite.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: State the immutable size ratio and exact contact surface; forbid full-size helper hands unless explicitly storyboarded.

examples.visible_symptom: Miniature engineers become full-size, androids become tiny heads, and named creators merge with the subject.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Restate exact relative scale and named-role appearance in every beat; include an unchanging physical scale reference in frame.

examples.repair: Add SameScene/NoCutaway guard and require final frame to retain original location and subject.

examples.visible_symptom: The model changes a decorative latte pattern instead of animating the requested face.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Define the target anatomy or object parts and the exact before/after action; forbid unrelated pattern morphing.

examples.visible_symptom: A title promises a sip or preparation action but frames only show a package reveal.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Require the named action in a defined beat with visible object, contact, and completion state.

examples.visible_symptom: Cosmic particle, roadway, car, and molecule appear as disconnected nouns rather than one causal sequence.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Choose one visual metaphor per generation and storyboard every semantic transition as a separate shot with a defined match cut.

examples.visible_symptom: Labels become gibberish, tiles reorder, charts redraw, and app icons mutate between frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock one referenced UI image; forbid new labels or logos; keep the screen fronto-parallel; validate OCR and tile positions before delivery.

examples.failure: Source watermark or provider mark in final frame
examples.visible_symptom: Small recurring mark at bottom right in 49 of 50 records.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Add a hard reject gate and rerender or crop only when composition-safe; never promote marked renders as gold.

examples.failure: Specific subject identity degrades to a generic class
examples.visible_symptom: Named curry leaves and Rafale aircraft are replaced by generic broad leaves or unstable fighter silhouettes.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Require reference-conditioned morphology and semantic identity review before accepting visual polish.

examples.visible_symptom: Five sampled frames are nearly identical despite a requested or category-expected action.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify measurable start and end composition deltas and reject outputs whose sampled-frame difference stays below threshold.

examples.visible_symptom: Several samples repeat the same composition or the subject exits early and does not return.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Define a visible state change for every beat and require subject coverage through the final sampled interval.

examples.visible_symptom: Five samples remain near-identical or show only a digital push.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Name one intrinsic moving element, its path, and its end state; fail QC when frame-difference evidence is absent.

examples.visible_symptom: Five samples remain nearly identical despite a requested action or camera move.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify start state, midpoint delta, end state, and minimum visible displacement.

examples.visible_symptom: Five samples remain virtually identical except for watermark or tiny camera drift.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify measurable product rotation, changing light sweep, interaction, or camera displacement and enforce a minimum motion-delta gate.

examples.failure: Static miniature diorama without visible work progress
examples.repair: Require tool contact plus before/after surface change in the same shot or adjacent frames.

examples.visible_symptom: Five temporal samples remain nearly identical despite a zoom, loop, dolly, compression, or cascade request.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Define start, midpoint, and end state deltas and require minimum pixel and semantic motion coverage.

examples.visible_symptom: The render establishes the chamber or problem but never shows the pour, insertion, smile, greeting, eye opening, or loop closure.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare a mandatory final-frame state and reserve the last beat for a held, verifiable payoff.

examples.visible_symptom: Several sampled frames repeat the same composition with no meaningful evolution.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Assign a visible state change, camera change, or subject action to every 2-3 second interval.

examples.visible_symptom: Steam, doors, or reflections move while the named subject does not perform the requested action.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify start pose, contact action, end pose, and object response for the named subject.

examples.visible_symptom: A static sculpture, diagonal structure, or glossy set replaces requested tearing, rippling, reconstruction, or tracking motion.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Define visible start, midpoint, and end geometry changes and require displacement of named surfaces.

examples.failure: Steam intersects liquid or becomes cloth-like
examples.visible_symptom: Opaque ribbons descend through the rim, spread on the beverage, or form overly regular decorative spirals.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Thin translucent vapor only, rising from the liquid surface, no downward flow, no surface penetration, and plume height below two vessel heights.

examples.visible_symptom: A requested five-shot montage produces only one or two visual modes.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Render each beat as a separately enumerated shot with a required acceptance frame, then assemble the montage.

examples.visible_symptom: A multi-action prompt resolves to one static cooking vignette.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Compile each requested action into a numbered shot or reject the prompt as overpacked for the duration.

examples.visible_symptom: Handshake precedes title, multiple scenes merge on one background, or the final walk-away never occurs.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Generate shots separately or enforce ordered hard-cut states with non-overlapping subject and background requirements.

examples.visible_symptom: Thirty-scene montage becomes one bedroom routine, 360-degree orbit stays frontal, or first frame carries no subject information.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Set minimum distinct environment and angle counts, sample checkpoints by beat, and reject low-information or repeated frames.

examples.visible_symptom: The sequence jumps from binary noise to sketch eye to glossy synthetic iris instead of evolving one coherent object.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: One rendering language, one eye geometry, continuous material evolution, no unrelated intermediate visual styles.

examples.visible_symptom: A singular animal prompt becomes multiple animals.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Exactly one sloth is visible; no second sloth, extra animal, duplicate head, or mirrored animal.

examples.visible_symptom: A recurring hiker or dinosaur disappears for later or middle sampled frames without a story reason.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Add subject_presence_lock for every beat and require explicit exit timing before the subject may leave frame.

examples.visible_symptom: A boxer-and-speed-bag prompt returns a seated person interacting with a bird.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use a first-frame subject reference and hard reject when required nouns and action are absent from the sampled frames.

examples.visible_symptom: Latte designs redraw, coffee develops bubbles without agitation, or drink color changes without a pour.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock surface topology, pattern, liquid color, level, and foam distribution; only steam may change.

examples.visible_symptom: Prongs enlarge, halos become uneven, chain rows repeat mechanically, or junctions become structurally implausible.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Lock stone cut, prong count, setting thickness, chain-row count, and connection points across all frames.

examples.failure: Synthetic UI and readable brand leakage
examples.visible_symptom: Prominent Chanel text or nonstandard app icons become the sharpest details in the frame.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use blank or deliberately abstract screens unless a verified interface reference is supplied; run OCR and icon-consistency checks before approval.

examples.visible_symptom: A creature changes from riding to standing or from land to water without a continuous transition.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: State one location, one route, and every required transition contact; split incompatible states into explicit shots.

examples.visible_symptom: Faces, watch models, vehicle body parts, or food portions change across sampled frames.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Declare immutable identity tokens and compare first, middle, and last checkpoints before accepting the render.

examples.visible_symptom: Missing words, malformed letters, extra characters, or changing dial/sign copy.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Reserve a clean text plate and composite exact vector typography after render; do not ask the image model to preserve small text through motion.

examples.visible_symptom: Gibberish headings, changing letterforms, or the wrong object paired with a learning letter.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Render exact text as a protected asset or overlay; validate every word and semantic pair before acceptance.

examples.visible_symptom: Plastic skin, unstable teeth and lips, elongated fingers, and silent singing become obvious in close-up.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Reduce facial crop, minimize visible hands, lock identity and mouth anatomy, constrain to one lyric-free expression beat, and require audio when singing remains visible.

examples.visible_symptom: Spoon, knife, fork, or spatula floats near the target or is controlled by the wrong actor.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Name both grip contact and tool-target contact; require both to remain visible in the same frame.

examples.visible_symptom: A named brick-toy prompt produces unmistakable proprietary visual language without provenance or license evidence.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use generic interlocking-brick character language unless approved brand assets and usage rights are attached.

examples.visible_symptom: Source material remains intact while the destination state appears abruptly or through a new pour source.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Show source-contact-intermediate-result as separate visible beats; forbid cuts, pre-existing destination material, and late source props.

examples.visible_symptom: A coherent scene abruptly changes framing, exposure, subject visibility, or product angle without a readable transition.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: One continuous camera move, or declare the cut and match direction, light, subject, and composition across the edit.

examples.visible_symptom: Subject, scale, and environment jump without a visible transformation bridge.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use an explicit cut or lock a single shared material and scale through the entire transition.

examples.visible_symptom: Diver mask, face, tank, suit markings, body proportions, and treasure placement change during the wide-to-close move.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use a fixed character sheet for front, back, mask, tank, gloves, and suit; lock one chest location and preserve gear through every shot scale.

examples.visible_symptom: A large foreground object appears late without a visible pickup or transition.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Show the prop in the establishing frame or include a continuous pickup beat before the hero insert.

examples.visible_symptom: Subject jumps from seated close-up to standing wide, or object count changes from one lens to two.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use one continuous shot or declare the edit; preserve subject pose, object count, and screen direction across the transition.

examples.visible_symptom: Flame appears without a strike, becomes an opaque ribbon, changes scale abruptly, or behaves like a fixed candle wick.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Specify ignition phases, flame attachment surface, maximum flame height, transparent edge behavior, smoke amount, and continuity hold.

examples.failure: Unreliable small text and brand labels
examples.visible_symptom: Labels, signs, scoreboards, or UI copy are too small or inconsistent to verify.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Render a text-free plate and composite approved vector or raster text in post at a minimum legible size.

examples.visible_symptom: Embossed marks and nib micro-lettering cannot be read or change shape.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use no branding by default; if text is required, lock exact approved text and validate it in every frame.

examples.visible_symptom: Pastry floats, paneer materializes, or chicken lifts and reforms without a hand or tool.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Show the actor or utensil before motion begins, preserve object count, and prohibit autonomous food movement.

examples.visible_symptom: Product boxes float screen-fixed, ignore perspective, or cover people without believable occlusion.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Use verified transparent packs with camera tracking, perspective scaling, and explicit foreground safe zones.

examples.failure: Visible corner mark or watermark leakage
examples.visible_symptom: Small changing glyphs or circular marks appear in the lower-right corner of 46 reviewed records.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Detect and reject marked frames before gold classification, or explicitly route provider watermarks to an authorized removal or clean-render workflow.

examples.failure: Visible generator watermark or bottom-edge overlay
examples.visible_symptom: Swirl logo and/or tick-like marks appear near the lower edge; every reviewed record was affected.

examples.visible_symptom: Small repeated symbols or barcode-like marks appear near lower corners.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Add no-logo/no-watermark guard and run a corner-region artifact detector before approval.

examples.visible_symptom: Barcode-like marks in early frames and circular marks in later frames contaminate otherwise clean pixels.
examples.repair_prompt_guard: Apply provider-safe clean-output settings or a validated removal/crop pass before gold classification.

examples.visible_symptom: A giant looks cinematic but its size is ambiguous because people or vehicles are absent.
